facts.claim: For 2027, New Year's Day (元旦) falls on Friday 1 January; the statutory holiday runs 1-3 January, 3 days, with no make-up workday.

For 2027, the Spring Festival holiday runs 5 February (the eve of the lunar new year, Friday) to 13 February (the eighth day of the first lunar month, Saturday) — 9 days, with 31 January (Sunday) and 14 February (Sunday) as make-up workdays.
For 2027, Qingming (清明节) runs 3-5 April (Saturday to Monday), 3 days, with no make-up workday.
For 2027, Labour Day runs 1-5 May (Saturday to Wednesday), 5 days, with 8 May (Saturday) as a make-up workday.
For 2027, the Dragon Boat Festival (端午节) is a single day off on 9 June (Wednesday) — not stitched to a weekend.
For 2027, the Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节) is a single day off on 15 September (Wednesday).
For 2027, the National Day holiday runs 1-7 October (Friday to Thursday), 7 days, with 26 September (Sunday) and 9 October (Saturday) as make-up workdays.
For 2026, New Year's Day (元旦) ran 1-3 January, 3 days, with 4 January (Sunday) as a make-up workday.

For 2026, the Spring Festival holiday ran 15 February (the 28th day of the 12th lunar month Sunday) to 23 February (the 7th day of the first lunar month, Monday) — 9 days, with 14 February and 28 February as make-up workdays.
For 2026, Qingming (清明节) ran 4-6 April (Saturday to Monday), 3 days, with no make-up workday.
For 2026, Labour Day ran 1-5 May (Friday to Tuesday), 5 days, with 9 May (Saturday) as a make-up workday.
For 2026, the Dragon Boat Festival (端午节) ran 19-21 June (Friday to Sunday), 3 days.
For 2026, the Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节) ran 25-27 September (Friday to Sunday), 3 days.
For 2026, the National Day holiday ran 1-7 October (Thursday to Wednesday), 7 days, with 20 September (Sunday) and 10 October (Saturday) as make-up workdays.

Since 1 January 2025, all citizens get 13 days of statutory public holiday a year: 1 day for New Year's Day, 4 days for Spring Festival, 1 day for Qingming, 2 days for Labour Day, 1 day for the Dragon Boat Festival, 1 day for Mid-Autumn and 3 days for National Day.

Spring Festival is a statutory holiday of 4 days — Lunar New Year's Eve plus the first to the third day of the first lunar month — set by the 2024 amendment to the national holiday measures, in force from 1 January 2025.
Labour Day is a statutory holiday of 2 days — 1 and 2 May — set by the same 2024 amendment, in force from 1 January 2025.
National Day is a statutory holiday of 3 days — 1 to 3 October — under the national holiday measures currently in force.
Except in special cases, the working stretch immediately before or after a public holiday is generally no more than 6 consecutive days — a rule added by the 2024 amendment.
The State Council published the List of Commonly Used Standard Chinese Characters (《通用规范汉字表》) by Notice No. 23 of 2013, dated 5 June 2013 and released 19 August 2013.

The 2013 table contains 8,105 characters in three tiers: 3,500 at the first tier (basic education), 3,000 at the second, and 1,605 at the third; the notice states that character use in general Chinese social life shall follow this table.
Chinese calligraphy was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2009 (ref. RL 00216).

China's official intangible-cultural-heritage documentation records calligraphy in the national nine-year compulsory curriculum, citing the Ministry of Education's Opinions on Calligraphy Education in Primary and Secondary Schools and the Guidelines for Calligraphy Education in Schools as the policy basis for survival.

China's traditional tea-processing techniques and associated social practices were inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List on 29 November 2022, at the 17th session of the Intergovernmental Committee held in Rabat, Morocco.

Chinese tea is divided into 6 categories - green, yellow, dark (hei), white, oolong and black (hong) - by processing and oxidation, with a further 2,000+ products once flower-scented and reprocessed teas are counted, the wording the Ministry of Culture and Tourism uses.
The tea-processing listing is the 44th item, by 44 related national-level intangible-heritage projects, and China had 43 UNESCO intangible-heritage listings before it, ranking first in the world.

The 24 solar terms (二十四节气) were inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List on 30 November 2016, at the 11th session in Addis Ababa; the element is framed as the time-knowledge system Chinese people built by observing the sun's annual motion.

The 24 solar terms were first added to the national intangible-heritage list in 2006, with sub-elements added in 2011 (Jiuhua Lichun rites, Banchun quannong, Shiqian shuo chun) and in 2014 (Sanmen jidong, Zhuang Shuangxiang festival, Miao Ganqiu, Anren ganfenshe).

Spring Festival - the social practices of the Chinese people in celebration of the traditional new year - was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List on 4 December 2024, at the 19th session in Asuncion, Paraguay.
With the Spring Festival listing, China had 44 items on UNESCO's intangible-heritage lists and registers, and the count stayed the highest in the world, as stated in the inscription report.

China's Spring Festival inscription is the 44th item on UNESCO's intangible-heritage lists - the Dragon Boat Festival (2009) and the 24 solar terms (2016) came before it, as the national intangible-heritage inventory records.
